evals.name: scaffold-dialogue-graph-tool
evals.prompt: I'm on Unity 6000.6.3f1. Scaffold a minimal Graph Toolkit tool for dialogue authoring: a DialogueGraph asset type with .dialogue extension, a menu item to create it, a StartNode, and a LineNode with a Speaker string, a Text string and a Next output. Show the C# files and where they go.
expectations: Defines a class deriving from Unity.GraphToolkit.Editor.Graph decorated with [Graph(...)] carrying the file extension and marked [Serializable]
Creates the asset through GraphDatabase.PromptInProjectBrowserToCreateNewAsset<DialogueGraph>() from a [MenuItem] static method
Node classes derive from Node, are [Serializable], and define ports by overriding OnDefinePorts with context.AddInputPort / AddOutputPort chains that end in .Build()
Places the files in an Editor-only assembly (an Editor folder or editor-only asmdef)
Does not use internal or legacy types such as GraphModel, NodeModel, GraphObject, GraphViewEditorWindow, Stencil, or UnityEditor.Experimental.GraphView
Does not instruct the user to install a com.unity.graphtoolkit package

Every Graph Toolkit member, attribute and type used in the code exists in the public API with the documented casing and signature: PascalCase properties such as FirstConnectedPort and IsConnected, positional attribute constructor arguments, Hash128 for element IDs, and no invented methods

evals.name: port-capacity-and-type-casting
evals.prompt: In my Graph Toolkit tool (Unity 6.6) the 'Next' output port on my nodes should only allow a single wire, and I want an int output to be connectable to a float input. How do I do both?
expectations: Uses .WithCapacity(PortCapacity.Single) in the port builder chain for the single-wire port
Overrides Graph.IsConnectionAllowed(IPort output, IPort input) and checks output.DataType and input.DataType to allow int to float
States or implies that the graph only records the connection and the conversion itself happens in the importer or runtime code
Does not invent builder methods such as SetCapacity, MaxConnections, AllowCast, or attributes for capacity

Every Graph Toolkit member, attribute and type used in the code exists in the public API with the documented casing and signature: PascalCase properties such as FirstConnectedPort and IsConnected, positional attribute constructor arguments, Hash128 for element IDs, and no invented methods

evals.name: state-machine-tool-with-conditions
evals.prompt: Unity 6000.7.0b4. Build an enemy AI state machine editor with Graph Toolkit's State Machine API: states Idle, Patrol and Chase, a float condition 'Distance to player' with a comparison dropdown, and a valueless 'Took damage' trigger condition. Also show how an importer would read the states, transitions and conditions into a runtime ScriptableObject.
expectations: Defines a class deriving from StateMachine decorated with [StateMachine(...)] and creates assets via StateMachineDatabase.PromptInProjectBrowserToCreateNewAsset
States derive from State and are [Serializable]; they do not define ports
The distance condition derives from Condition<float> and overrides DisplayComparisonDropdown to return true; the trigger derives from the non-generic Condition
The importer loads with StateMachineDatabase.LoadStateMachineForImporter and walks GetStates(), GetOutgoingTransitions(), GetRules() and each rule's RootCondition
Handles IGroupCondition and IVariableCondition when compiling the condition tree, not only the custom condition types

Builds on the State Machine API types (StateMachine, State, Condition, ITransition, ITransitionRule) rather than emulating a state machine with Graph, Node, ContextNode or BlockNode, and does not use internal types such as StateModel, TransitionModel, GraphModel or ConditionModel

Every Graph Toolkit member, attribute and type used in the code exists in the public API with the documented casing and signature: PascalCase properties such as FirstConnectedPort and IsConnected, positional attribute constructor arguments, Hash128 for element IDs, and no invented methods

evals.name: importer-to-runtime-asset
evals.prompt: I have a Graph Toolkit graph type QuestGraph with extension 'quest' and nodes StartNode, ObjectiveNode (string input 'Title', output 'Next') and EndNode. Write the ScriptedImporter that produces a QuestRuntime ScriptableObject listing the objectives in order, and explain how the runtime assembly must be set up.
expectations: Uses [ScriptedImporter(version, "quest")] on a ScriptedImporter subclass and loads the graph with GraphDatabase.LoadGraphForImporter<QuestGraph>(ctx.assetPath)
Finds the entry node with GetNodes().OfType<StartNode>() and follows connections through GetOutputPortByName(...).FirstConnectedPort and GetNode()
Reads the objective title from the input port with TryGetValue when the port is unconnected and resolves the upstream node through FirstConnectedPort when it is connected
Adds the runtime object with ctx.AddObjectToAsset and makes it the main object with ctx.SetMainObject
States that the runtime assembly must not reference Unity.GraphToolkit.Editor and that the importer lives in an Editor assembly
Handles a null graph or a missing StartNode without throwing

Every Graph Toolkit member, attribute and type used in the code exists in the public API with the documented casing and signature: PascalCase properties such as FirstConnectedPort and IsConnected, positional attribute constructor arguments, Hash128 for element IDs, and no invented methods

evals.name: version-gate-state-machine-on-6-6
evals.prompt: We're on Unity 6000.6.1f1 and want to build an Animator-like state machine editor for our AI using Graph Toolkit. Give me the StateMachine and State classes to start with.
expectations: States clearly that the Graph Toolkit State Machine API requires Unity 6000.7 or newer and is not available on 6000.6
Does not present StateMachine, State or Condition<T> code as if it compiles on 6000.6
Offers a concrete way forward, such as upgrading to 6000.7 or modelling states as regular Graph nodes on 6000.6, and asks or notes which the user prefers
Does not suggest installing a package to obtain the State Machine API

evals.name: graph-changed-delta-and-validation
evals.prompt: Graph Toolkit, Unity 6.6. When the user edits my graph I need to (a) show an error marker on any ObjectiveNode whose Title is empty and (b) react only to nodes that were added or removed instead of scanning everything. How?
expectations: Overrides Graph.OnGraphChanged(GraphLogger logger) and reports with logger.LogError(message, node) so the marker is attached to the offending node
States that the GraphLogger.GraphChanges / ChangeKind change delta exists only from Unity 6000.7 and is not available on the user's 6.6 Editor

For 6.6, proposes a working alternative to a full rescan, such as caching node IDs (Hash128) in a non-serialized set on the graph and diffing against GetNodes() each call, and notes that title edits on existing nodes still need checking
Warns that the graph must not be modified inside OnGraphChanged and that modifications belong in a GraphLogAction, menu item or importer
Does not use graphViewChanged, GraphViewChange, or other GraphView-era APIs

Every Graph Toolkit member, attribute and type used in the code exists in the public API with the documented casing and signature: PascalCase properties such as FirstConnectedPort and IsConnected, positional attribute constructor arguments, Hash128 for element IDs, and no invented methods
